question: Can a server exchange two existing factual associations by changing the country and adjacent punctuation in its old attention cache, without running the updated document? The local donor oracle matched 40/48 changed answers and kept all stable original top tokens. A zero-donor value swap controlled 27/48. Calibrate a map from the old source-minus-target vectors to the true local counterfactual displacement on other documents before any questions. At test, the only update information supplied is which two country-token rows should exchange their content. All other cache coordinates and recurrent states stay fixed.
calibration: 96 fixed new prompt IDs 64932000..64932095, both original DEFAULT and WORK templates, all three role pairs cycled using seed modulo three. Run full old and transposed document prefixes at calibration time. No trailing questions, labels, native query answers, decoded outputs or future test data enter fitting. Compute separate means for every template, role, key/value head, token offset and layer from old documents. Remove rotary position phase from attention keys before fitting and restore it after transfer. Learn independently for each layer, K/V channel, token offset (country/next punctuation), and KV head. The source difference is (source vector minus source role mean) minus (target vector minus target role mean). The supervised change is the exact new target vector minus its old vector. A rank-32 output basis is fitted from these paired displacements. Fit a ridge map from source differences onto its 32 coefficients (ridge .02 times mean Gram diagonal). Apply the resulting paired factorization to the old target. No tuning of rank, scale or gates. The vectors retain the model's original cache dtype after the edit.
comparators: Stale, full updated prompt, text correction, raw V-only exchange, role-centered K/V exchange, and the simpler orthogonal projection of the same centered source differences onto the paired displacement basis. Include the ideal actual donor K/V at all four rows, and an executable comparator that reevaluates each two-token edit in its own unmodified old prefix checkpoint while keeping all other cached coordinates. The latter is a localized selective recomputation control. Compare whole-vocabulary next tokens for all three future queries.
development: All 12 exposed pilot IDs and 24 documents; 48 changed and 24 stable questions. Promote the learned map only if it loses at most two full-replay successes, preserves every stable answer originally correct, gains at least 4 changed answers over plain value exchange, gains at least two over both role-mean exchange and paired orthogonal projection, and matches or exceeds the total number correct with localized recomputation. No selection by native confidence or clean-correct cases.
confirmation: Only after promotion, run 48 fresh document IDs 64934000..64934047 with both templates and three queries. Confirm if it misses none of full replay's correct changed or stable questions, preserves all original-correct stable answers, and beats every zero-donor simple exchange control with positive seed-clustered intervals. Charge initial ingest and the three actual answers plus the edit for end-to-end cost versus checkpoint replay, correction notice and localized recomputation. Report calibration wall time and break-even. For this short-corpus workload even a zero-token update can save only 15.4% of full layer-token positions versus an ideal prefix checkpoint, as measured in development. A larger number of facts or updates would require a distinct prospective scalability study.
limits: Local Apple M5 only. 12 minutes calibration, 12 minutes development, 40 minutes conditional confirmation. One implementation repair. A positive screen alone supports no end-to-end speed or unrestricted editing claim.
